$comment: Feature workflow (D3): define -> design -> implement -> test -> deploy -> close. JSON (not YAML) because hooks are bash and jq is available. Read this with jq, e.g. `jq '.phases[] | select(.phase=="define")' feature.json`. Phases are listed in run order; `order` is 1-based and matches array position. `owner_agent` is the plugin agent that owns the phase's artifact (D4) — only that agent may write it (REQ-005). `artifact` is the filename inside the session folder that phase creates/owns, or null for Close, which produces no session file (D1). An `artifact` ending in `/` is a folder artifact (#23 DES-020, D13): one artifact with one owner, frozen as a unit, whose fixed file set is `artifact_files` (files one level inside the folder, nothing deeper). `legacy_artifact` is the root path past sessions use for the same phase; they're never migrated (D6), so it stays in the allowlist, and the guard lets a session use one layout or the other, never both. `milestone` is the name shown to the user at the milestone gate and used in gh comments (D5); `gh_label` is the label applied while that phase is active. `conversational` marks phases that talk to the user directly through the orchestrator (Define, Design) vs. phases that mostly execute (D3 main loop, D4). `framing` is what this session type plugs into the shared framing skill (skills/framing/SKILL.md, #23 DES-007): `run_in_phase` names the phase that runs framing (the framing skill itself names no phase), `produces` is that phase's artifact, `standards` are the standards skills that apply, `type_file` is the `types/{type_file}.md` each standards skill reads, and `tiers` are the depth tiers this type allows. The guard hook doesn't read `framing`.
